chunks.content: # CLO Master Express Lesson 20: Live Special Tutorial on Denim Washing This document provides detailed instructions and technical insights on creating realistic denim washing effects in CLO 3D, including pattern import and adjustment, sewing techniques, fabric application, water wash effects, texture processing, and grading functions. It covers practical workflows, software tools, and tips for simulating authentic denim garments. --- ## 1. Model and Pattern Import with Panel Arrangement This section explains how to import a model and adjust pattern panels for proper fit, focusing on waist size adjustment, symmetry settings, panel positioning, and alignment using CLO tools. - Import the model and adjust the waist size if the model's waist is wider than the sample. - Import the sample pattern and set all symmetrical panels as left-right symmetrical. - Open the baseline of the sample pattern and position it to avoid model obstruction. - Use the positioning ball aligned with world coordinates to level panels. - Employ the arrangement point tool to quickly place panels on corresponding points of the model. - Adjust panel positions along the X and Y axes in the property editor for precise fit. - For the back of the model, arrange panels to avoid serious penetration by widening them slightly. - Apply the counterfeit tool to the waist post panel for proper simulation. - Ensure waist area piccons (small tabs or tacks) are parallel and correctly positioned in front of the buckle. - Use the quick arrangement tool for small panels such as hem front doors and Hamburg belts. - Temporarily place small panels on top before sewing. - Sew small panels using internal sewing lines, changing the sewing line type to "Turn" for fold effects. - Manage layer relationships with the layer setting tool to ensure stable simulation. --- ## 2. Sewing Techniques and Foldable Model Creation This section covers sewing panel assembly, foldable model creation, and simulation tips. - Sew panels together with internal sewing lines, setting the sewing line type to "Turn." - For foldable models (e.g., long panels), use internal cables and sewing lines to create fold effects. - Simulate after sewing, adjust and pull panels as needed, then remove temporary sewing lines to finalize folds. - Use keyboard shortcuts (Shift + Q) to hide patterns during arrangement. - Add buckles on the waist and rotate their direction in the attribute editor. - Use the buckle button in the 3D window to attach buckles properly. - Sewing speed can be increased if the focus is less on detailed sewing accuracy. --- ## 3. Fabric Application and Double-Layer Waistband Construction This section focuses on fabric selection, application, and construction of a double-layer waistband for better realism. - Select denim fabric from the CLO library and apply it to the pants. - Reuse fabrics already applied by adding them to the fabric library. - Sew a leather label made of sheepskin fabric onto the back of the pants.

Fabric Application and Double-Layer Waistband Construction This section focuses on fabric selection, application, and construction of a double-layer waistband for better realism. - Select denim fabric from the CLO library and apply it to the pants. - Reuse fabrics already applied by adding them to the fabric library. - Sew a leather label made of sheepskin fabric onto the back of the pants. - Construct a double-layer waistband to improve durability and realism; the inner fabric texture will differ from the outer. - For the crotch area, create a small fold using the folding arrangement tool: - Expand the outer line of the fabric. - Draw an inner line for the shoulder strap. - Harden the fabric. - Manually set the folding angle to zero degrees. - Sew and adjust the sewing line length. - Simulate to finalize the fold. - The waist panel has a double structure with sewing positions approximately 2 mm inside; add an internal sewing line accordingly. - Add fabric thickness to simulate double layers. --- ## 4. Merging Corners and Creating Sewing Edges This section details techniques for merging fabric corners and simulating sewing edges. - Merge fabric corners to replicate the original pattern effect. - After merging, hook the baseline to maintain folding effects. - Set folding angles and delete inner sewing support lines post-merging. - Create a small strip (5 mm width) to simulate the sewing edge structure. - Measure and sew this strip on the sides of the pants, changing the sewing line type to "Turn." - Manually reduce the strip’s diameter and conflict thickness as needed. - Add the strip to the inside of the pants. - Simulate symmetrical strips on both sides. - Adjust width, thickness, and color (e.g., golden brown) of the strips. - Correct eyelet orientations by rotating 180 degrees and adjusting width and color. - Add nail effects to small panels using twist tools: - Select nail patterns. - Adjust nail width. - Place nails on panels. - Use white texture display for clarity. - Copy to parallel panels to avoid duplication. - Adjust material and color for nails. - Fine-tune nail line positions. --- ## 5. Denim Texture and Water Wash Effect Preparation This section explains scanning, processing, and applying denim textures and water wash effects for realistic garment simulation. - Denim texture consists of superimposed fabrics with different textures on the front and back. - Water wash techniques affect front and back textures differently. - Scan larger fabric areas (150–300 dpi recommended) to ensure even color and texture. - Use third-party software like Pixplant and Photoshop for processing: - Create four-sided continuous fabric patterns. - Remove irregularities and fix color discrepancies. - Adjust colors to closely match actual fabric. - Use Photoshop’s color interface with three adjustment triangles to lighten or darken texture images. - Save processed textures as PNG files with transparency.

Detailed Water Wash Effect Creation Workflow This section outlines the process to create realistic water wash effects on denim edges and seams using CLO tools and Photoshop. - Water wash effects vary by seam type, including side seams, inner seams, single needle lines, crotch, and waist. - Use the sewing wrinkle tool in CLO to add water wash wrinkles. - Workflow to prepare water wash texture: - Scan denim fabric, especially seams like crotch. - Use Photoshop to create a square continuous texture. - Convert image to black and white by removing color for easier selection. - Delete unwanted textures using the sewing wrinkle tool. - Fill selected areas with black on new layers. - Apply filters (Gaussian blur) for smooth continuous effect. - Adjust color curves to make white areas brighter. - Save as transparent PNG for use as a sewing wrinkle pattern. - In CLO, add the water wash pattern using the sewing wrinkle tool along seams and edges. - Adjust parameters: - Width (default ~1 cm, e.g., 1.2 cm for pants). - Transparency (view in rendering window for accurate lighting). - Density (100% means original texture; less than 100% increases density). - Switch fabric material to denim for correct rendering. - Adjust line drawing and texture transparency iteratively for best effect.

Denim Texture and Water Wash Effect Preparation This section explains scanning, processing, and applying denim textures and water wash effects for realistic garment simulation. - Denim texture consists of superimposed fabrics with different textures on the front and back. - Water wash techniques affect front and back textures differently. - Scan larger fabric areas (150–300 dpi recommended) to ensure even color and texture. - Use third-party software like Pixplant and Photoshop for processing: - Create four-sided continuous fabric patterns. - Remove irregularities and fix color discrepancies. - Adjust colors to closely match actual fabric. - Use Photoshop’s color interface with three adjustment triangles to lighten or darken texture images. - Save processed textures as PNG files with transparency. - Apply fabric textures to pants in CLO, including hairline textures for stitching details. - Verify that pattern surfaces are correctly oriented; reverse if necessary. - Use the hairline picture to simulate top-stitching effects with adjustable thickness, color (e.g., copper yellow), and spacing. - Apply single and double-edged hairlines for different sewing effects. - For side seams, create binding lockstitch effects by: - Creating a new hairline type. - Selecting overlock stitch. - Changing mesh face to "All" for front and back visibility. - Add bartack hairlines on internal lines with zero spacing and custom colors. - Hairlines can be set as asymmetrical in CLO version 6.2. - Use internal lines to add decorative name lines on pockets and leather labels. --- ## 6. Leather Label Creation and Texture Editor Usage This section details creating a leather label and applying custom textures. - Use default sheepskin fabric for the leather label. - Use the texture editor tool to import logo patterns (e.g., CLO U logo). - Resize, fold (front and back), and flatten the label in 3D. - Rotate texture direction for proper alignment. - Flattening reveals bottom leather texture. - Add name lines on both front and inner sides. --- ## 7. Detailed Water Wash Effect Creation Workflow This section outlines the process to create realistic water wash effects on denim edges and seams using CLO tools and Photoshop. - Water wash effects vary by seam type, including side seams, inner seams, single needle lines, crotch, and waist. - Use the sewing wrinkle tool in CLO to add water wash wrinkles. - Workflow to prepare water wash texture: - Scan denim fabric, especially seams like crotch. - Use Photoshop to create a square continuous texture. - Convert image to black and white by removing color for easier selection. - Delete unwanted textures using the sewing wrinkle tool. - Fill selected areas with black on new layers. - Apply filters (Gaussian blur) for smooth continuous effect. - Adjust color curves to make white areas brighter. - Save as transparent PNG for use as a sewing wrinkle pattern. - In CLO, add the water wash pattern using the sewing wrinkle tool along seams and edges. - Adjust parameters: - Width (default ~1 cm, e.g., 1.2 cm for pants). - Transparency (view in rendering window for accurate lighting). - Density (100% means original texture; less than 100% increases density). - Switch fabric material to denim for correct rendering. - Adjust line drawing and texture transparency iteratively for best effect. - Apply water wash patterns symmetrically on both sides after disabling symmetry. - Hairlines complement water wash by simulating light reflections and wrinkles. - Rename materials for easier management. --- ## 8. Partial Water Wash and Hole Effects: Methods and Application This section describes two methods to create partial water wash and hole effects on denim. ### Method 1: Texture Stickers - Use CLO's library (Hardware and Trims folder) containing washing textures. - Add textures as stickers on the pants. - Adjust position, size, and transparency in 2D and 3D views. - Transparency requires checking in rendering for shadow accuracy. - Mirror stickers on symmetrical panels. - Stickers do not create actual holes; they overlay visual effects. ### Method 2: Texture Board Application - Duplicate the existing denim fabric and rename. - In print mode, widen or narrow the texture area for comparison. - Set resolution around 144–150 dpi to balance quality and file size. - Outline the pattern and hook the baseline. - Save and refresh the fabric board. - Use Photoshop to: - Create white shapes and blur them for hole effects. - Adjust color and blur radius for natural appearance. - Save as transparent PNG and replace original texture. - Apply hole texture to fabric board in CLO. - Use the multi-selection tool in Photoshop to remove texture pixels where holes are needed. - Process front and back textures separately, as back fabric texture is only visible in 2D window. - Decode layers in Photoshop to ensure transparency works correctly in CLO. - Save and refresh textures in CLO for hole effect visualization in rendering. --- ## 9.
